limits: Needs the network; the sequence leaves the machine.
E-values are relative to the database searched.
bio.jane/contract.noScientificClaim: Relays the remote service's own result unchanged; it computes no number of its own, so the service is the authority for what comes back.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which public sequences resemble this one, with what E-values?

description: Search a sequence against NCBI BLAST+ at EMBL-EBI (blastn, blastp, blastx, tblastn or tblastx) over ENA, UniProtKB, PDB and the vector-screening sets. This is the similarity search a methods section cites: it turns an unnamed span into named homologues with E-values, and hands the hits, the tabular report and the job id downstream. The sequence LEAVES THE MACHINE.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

databases.description: database ids to search, as the service names them (em_rel, uniprotkb, pdb, emvec…). Several are searched together. Left empty, the service's OWN default for this program's context is used and reported back.

email.description: EBI requires a contact address on every submission (their abuse contact, not a login). Left empty, the one saved in any EMBL-EBI panel is used.

feature.description: the feature's name, matched case-insensitively on the open record. Only applies when region is feature.

parameters.description: every other advertised parameter, one `id=value` per line, using the service's own ids (exp, matrix, filter, gapopen, gapext, wordsize, alignments, scores, taxids…). Left empty each keeps the service's default for this context. An id the service does not advertise is refused by name rather than dropped.

program.description: which BLAST program. The QUERY alphabet is derived from it and never asked for: blastx takes DNA and searches protein, tblastn the reverse. Values: blastn (blastn · dna query), blastp (blastp · protein query), blastx (blastx · dna query), tblastn (tblastn · protein query), tblastx (tblastx · dna query).

region.description: which part of the open record to search, when no sequence is wired in. Values: whole (the whole record), selection (the current selection), feature (a named feature).

sequence.description: the query. Wire a record or a sequence output, or paste raw/FASTA. Left empty, the region below is taken from the open record.

name: blast_search

hits.description: every hit, with its HSPs, accession, organism and the links the service sent

jobId.description: the dispatcher job id: what a methods section cites and what re-fetches this exact result

provenance.description: the binary, the command line EBI ran, the databases as built, and the search space the E-values are relative to

sequences.description: the hit subjects as FASTA, ready to wire straight into an alignment or a tree

tabular.description: the hits as BLAST's own outfmt 6 table, for download or a downstream parser

topCoverage.description: what fraction of the query the best hit covers, 0–1

topExpect.description: the best hit's E-value; wire into a $when to branch on significance

topHit.description: the best hit by E-value: what a "what is this?" step reads

topIdentity.description: percent identity of the best hit's best HSP
